display._note: One uniform mid-grey for every screen, so the eye is adapted to the same luminance throughout. sRGB 176 is ~2x the linear luminance of sRGB 128, and 0 is black, so dark and bright dots/checks balance around the background in linear light (nominal, uncalibrated monitor).

sizing._note: Author, 2026-10-14: no viewing distance and no visual angle. One reference layout at 1920 x 1080 physical pixels, scaled uniformly by s = min(W / 1920, H / 1080), W x H the full-screen window's physical (backing-store) pixels, so the operating system's display scaling and the browser zoom change nothing on the screen (2560 x 1440: s = 1.33; 3840 x 2160: 2; 2880 x 1800: 1.5, its width deciding; 2560 x 1080: 1). A degree of this file is reference_px_per_deg reference pixels: 44.3, the median of the 21 recorded Exp1 runs at their card-measured scale (physical px per degree), so at s = 1 the dot field of 5.4 deg is about 239 px, a dot of 0.32 deg about 14.2 px across, the scaling arc of 7.5 deg about 332 px in radius; the number line is spaces.count.length_reference_px. Every online run's geometry is this layout (source pixel; src/core/units.ts).

cloud._note: DeWind et al. (2015) size/spacing scheme. For a count N, log Size (= log item area + log total area) and log Spacing (= log field area + log sparsity) are drawn independently of N, so N is uncorrelated with Size, Spacing and coverage. Item area, field area, total area and density then necessarily co-vary with N and are recorded as covariates.

fixation._note: The combined bullseye and cross-hair target of Thaler et al. (2013). Shown during the inter-trial interval in `srgb` (black); during the pre-cue (timing.fixation_ms) it keeps its size and takes `pre_stimulus_srgb` (author, 2026-10-02: colour only, no size change), so its change of colour is the fixed warning before the cloud; removed at cloud onset. After a miss it is shown once in missing_response.missing_rgb (the yellow mark). Author, 2026-10-16: sized for stable fixation as in Thaler, Schuetz, Goodale and Gegenfurtner (2013, Vision Research 76, 31-42), the bullseye with the cross hair: an outer disc of 0.6 deg, the cross hair in the background colour, an inner disc of 0.2 deg, the cross hair as wide as the inner disc (0.2 deg); in pixels from an assumed typical setup of about 40 px per degree at the 1920 x 1080 reference (about 60 cm from a 24-inch monitor): outer 24 px, inner and cross hair 8 px, written here in this file's degrees (display.sizing: 44.3 reference px each): 24 / 44.3 = 0.5418 and 8 / 44.3 = 0.1806, so the pixel sizing rule scales them like every other size. The same mark on every screen that draws it (interval, pre-cue in pre_stimulus_srgb, estimation, betting, practice feedback, yellow mark after a miss).

feature_assignment._note: Wave 12 (author, 2026-10-19; generator schedule-2.0.0, config/design/stimulus_set/schedules_balanced.json): Size and Spacing are each split into thirds of their log range. Six main blocks: every (level x exposure) cell once per block; over the six blocks a cell shows six different images, each size third twice and each spacing third twice; in every block each image appears 3 or 4 times, each third 10 times, and a level's two cells show different images. The order of the main blocks is permuted per participant. The practice (train set): practice A, B and C of 10 trials (together every cell once; each part one short and one long cell of every band of three consecutive levels) and practice blocks 1 and 2 of every cell; a level's six practice trials show six different images, each third twice. spaces._note: The two response widgets (author, 2026-10-03, decisions 76-78). count = the number line of the estimation response and the betting range (absolute space, values are counts): a horizontal line 3 degrees above the screen centre (y_offset_deg -3, no random shift), length_reference_px reference pixels long (2026-10-14: 1056 = 0.55 x 1920, so the line of 1920 x 1080 on every window of at least that size, a wide 2560 x 1080 one too; before, length_fraction_of_width 0.55 of the stage width, Exp1 revision 2), 8 to 76 so that its middle is 42 (the mirror centre of the two contexts), no ticks and no labels; the estimation response is snapped to an integer (point_snap) and the betting ends too (interval_snap); probe_number writes the integer under the cursor above the preview disc on the named phases only (the estimation screen; the betting screen shows no number). rho = the scaling arc of the scaling response (relative space, values in [0, 1]): a half circle of radius_deg around the screen centre, always centred there, whose orientation (the angle of its middle) is drawn per trial from the trial seed and recorded, 'Smaller' and 'Larger' at its ends (end_labels), values growing from the 'Smaller' end to the 'Larger' end in `direction`. A line is shape 'line' (length, height, shift); an arc is shape 'arc' (radius, span, orientation, direction); a key of the other shape is refused. binarized._note: pilot_bsr (author 2026-10-26, decisions 3, 12, 13; revised 2026-10-27): S = 2 q_t - sum q_j^2 with q_j = coins on bin j / 20 (the tokens; 25 before 2026-10-28) and t the true count's bin of the 7 bins of 5 counts centred on the estimate (a true count outside the +-17 space: q_t = 0); P_stack = clip(a + b S, 0, 1), a = 0.30, b = 0.90 (2026-10-27, after the reward-design reviews (Fable item 1, Codex item 1); first calibrated to 0.25 / 1.25, under which every belief of SD <= 5.5 counts had the same 3-bin optimum; a = b = 0.5 is the original binarized quadratic rule (1 + S) / 2); P_rel = clip(1 - c (rho_hat - rho)^2, 0, 1), c = 4 (Fable item 2, Codex item 3; first 10): 0 from an error of 0.5; with the clip both rules are only approximately proper: under the stack rule the exact optimum (exact search over every stack, the first coin fixed) widens with a centred Gaussian belief's SD from 2.5 to 12 counts and is contiguous there (20 coins; 2.6 to 12 with 25), but a belief narrower than about 2.5 counts gains up to 0.004 by asymmetric outer coins; the relative estimate's mean is the best report whenever the belief over rho spans at most 0.5; a missed response, or one not run after an earlier miss, has probability 0. An incomplete stack (fewer than 20 coins at the time-out, review 2026-10-26 item 1) is paid 0 (win_probability.stack_paid); its formula value and S are kept (stack_formula, stack_score, stack_incomplete). Bonus (review item 2: one lottery, not two independent prizes): base 4 pounds; 5 main trials drawn at the end; one prize of 4.00 won with probability sum over the 5 drawn trials of (0.60 P_stack_paid + 0.20 P_rel) / 4, in [0, 1]; maximum bonus 4.00. The visible stack is a constrained report (review item 3): only the +-17 space can hold coins and a count outside it scores q_t = 0; analyse it as a constrained, quantised report, never its visible width as the full uncertainty, and the slide claims no more than that. typical: the assumptions of the expected bonus (author 2026-10-27, wave 12): estimate_error_bins = the shares of true count - estimate in the 7 bins of 5 counts centred on the estimate (-17 ... 17) and beyond them, by exposure (long [0.04, 0.08, 0.20, 0.34, 0.23, 0.07, 0.02], outside 0.03; short [0.01, 0.04, 0.07, 0.22, 0.21, 0.20, 0.12], outside 0.14; each sums to 1.01 by rounding and is normalised where read); a calibrated participant places the exact best whole-coin stack under the deployed clipped rule (the first coin on the middle bin; 20 coins, 2026-10-28: short [1, 1, 2, 5, 4, 4, 3], long [1, 2, 4, 7, 5, 1, 0]; with 25 coins short [1, 2, 2, 6, 6, 5, 3], long [1, 2, 5, 8, 6, 2, 1]); relative_abs_error_median 0.134, read as zero-mean Gaussian errors for the expected P_rel. Uncertainty_BSR_v2 (author 2026-10-29): t is the true count's bin of the 9 bins of 5 counts centred on the estimate (-22 ... 22; a true count outside: q_t = 0; a bin whose counts are all at or below 0 can hold no coin and never the true count); on 9 bins the exact optimum still widens with a centred Gaussian belief's SD from 2.5 to 12 counts and is contiguous there; typical on 9 bins (typical._note_2026_10_29): the exact best stacks short [0, 0, 1, 2, 4, 4, 4, 3, 2] (P_stack 0.436), long [0, 1, 2, 4, 7, 5, 1, 0, 0] (0.494), mean 0.465 (0.463 on 7 bins); the exact search covers C(27, 8) = 2,220,075 stacks, about 40 ms each.

On a screen whose cursor starts at the centre nothing marks a value and no click is taken until the cursor is reveal_after_move_deg from its start (decision 78). input_lockout_ms: presses during this time after a response screen appears are ignored and counted. Every points number - the live number of the betting screen, the feedback lines and the deduction beside the yellow mark - is coloured by its sign: above 0 in points_positive_rgb (green), below 0 in points_negative_rgb (red), 0 in the text grey (author, 2026-10-02 evening). body.text: Each trial has four parts: the dots, then your estimation, your betting coins and your relative estimate.
1 practice block and {n_main_blocks} main blocks of {trials_per_block} trials, about {listed_minutes} minutes. **Payment: {currency}{base}, plus up to {currency}{bonus_max} from lottery tickets.**
Keep your eyes on the centre mark. The dots appear there.
Order: the centre mark, then the dots flash briefly, then a noise pattern covers them.
Next you will see which numbers of dots appear in this experiment: first their distribution, then example pictures.
Type how many dots you think were shown, then **press Enter** within {estimation_s} seconds.
**Typing alone is not an answer: your number counts only after you press Enter.**
**No Enter in time: the trial ends there and its ticket cannot win.**
Type your **estimate** of the number of dots on the keyboard and press [pill]Enter[/pill] within [pill]{estimation_s} s[/pill].
Place your **betting range** on the numbers where you expect to win points: click its two ends, then click the button with the points. The range must include your estimate.
The line goes through your estimate, with a small mark every 5. Further right or higher means more dots.
Use two separate clicks, one at each end, not a double click.
If the correct answer falls inside your betting range, it wins points: the narrower the range, the more points, up to [green]{range_max_points}[/green]. The number on the button shows them.
Adjust your betting range to how sure you are of the number, so that you earn as many points as possible.
In practice blocks, the place of the [green]correct answer[/green] is shown on the line: [green]green[/green] when it is inside your betting range, [red]red[/red] when it is not.
Practice points are not paid.
Place all {stack_tokens} coins on the {n_bins} groups around your number.
• Click: 1 coin.
• Hold: more coins.
• Right-click or Backspace: take one off.

blocks._note: The blocks of a session (decision 1.5): the train blocks first in their stored order, then the test blocks in the participant's seeded order (src/design/order.ts), 30 trials each. A block names the trial type its trials run directly: entry k of train_trial_types is the trial type of stored train block k (so the list has one entry per train block of every context's schedule; the loader checks it), and every test block runs test_trial_type. A run is what the experiment page shows in one sitting: session = the whole session (all train blocks, all test blocks); pilot = the three train blocks and the first test block of the participant's order (author, 2026-10-02 evening: every block kind of the session is tried in the pilot). train_block_indices are stored train block indices and run in stored order; n_test_blocks keeps the first that many test blocks of the order. The intro screen before each block shows the picture of the session context's count distribution (show_distribution, distribution_picture; decision 64) and its Start button becomes active after intro_min_ms; after Start the first trial's black interval lasts lead_in_ms (decision 75). The block clock (align_trials; decisions 56, 62): every trial's pre-cue has a fixed target, the block origin + k x the fixed trial length + timing.iti_ms, so all unused time goes to the next inter-trial interval and every cloud comes at its fixed time; a lateness above clock_reset_after_ms re-sets the origin at that trial, a smaller one is recovered in the next interval. Between blocks the rest screen's button becomes active after rest_min_ms (author, 2026-09-30: at least 5 s). block_total = the rest screen shows the points of the block just finished and the end screen the paid total and its conversion; test blocks show no feedback after a trial, only this total. stop_rule (author, 2026-10-03, decision 84): in a block of block_kinds, the trial that brings the block's misses to max_misses ends the block and the run at once (after its yellow mark); no later trial or block runs, the stop screen (text.screen_stopped) shows, and the record is saved and downloaded as at a normal end, with status stopped; the run is paid reward.payment.base x the blocks completed before the stopping block / the blocks of the run, without a bonus; null = no stop. Revised 2026-10-04: the instruction slides are placed by the instructions section; block screens name the kinds Exercise and Main block (decision 118). Wave 12 (author, 2026-10-19): the session follows blocks.sequence: practice A (trial type estimation, 10 trials), practice B (estimation_betting, 10), practice C (scaling, 10), practice block 1 (full, 30, feedback), three main blocks, practice block 2 (full, 30, feedback), three main blocks; 270 trials, 180 of them in main blocks; the main blocks are the participant's order of the six stored test blocks. Estimation: at least 50 % of the estimates are multiples of 10 (estimate_rounding); the same number 5 times in a row (estimate_same_run) or on at least 33 % of the estimates (estimate_same_share); median estimation response time below 500 ms, treated as programmatic input (estimation_median_rt: the typed estimate's Enter from the screen's onset, the export's e_a_rt_ms); mean |estimate - count| above 20 dots (estimation_error); Spearman of the estimate with the count below 0.2 (estimate_rank_correlation). Scaling task: the 0-1 range in 10 equal bins, one bin with at least 50 % of the relative estimates (scaling_bin_share); mean |relative estimate - true percentile cell.rho| above 0.35 (scaling_error); Spearman with the true percentile below 0.05 (scaling_rank_correlation). Missed responses are left out of every value and denominator (estimation rules on the answered estimates, the coin rule on the answered stacks, an incomplete stack counted by its coins, scaling rules on the answered relative estimates; a missed estimate does not break a run of the same number); a rule with fewer than min_answered (10) answered responses fails. On the v1 practice block (Uncertainty raw/behavior/numerosity_bsr_v1, valid split of the v1 sanity check) this set would have stopped 7 of the 10 invalid and 3 of the 9 valid participants.
